Amy Barry-Macaulay.summary: Barry-Macaulay is a lawyer, has worked in the health, education, and environment sectors, and has been a chief of staff to a federal MP.

Phillip Schuhmann.summary: Schuhmann is a farmer and music teacher, and also owns and operates an arborist business. He has lived in the Strzlecki Ranges his entire life.

Mazen John.summary: John migrated to Australia from Iraq during the First Gulf War and speaks four languages. He has worked as a security guard, in quality control for Ford and Toyota, and is currently a full time carer for his daughter.

Wayne Hutchinson.summary: Hutchinson’s professional life began in his family business in Heidelberg West and he has gone on to operate businesses in Greensborough, Richmond and Geelong.

Eddie Dadisho.prior_occupation: compliance manager in the banking sector
Eddie Dadisho.summary: Dadisho has finance and law degrees from Western Sydney University and is a compliance manager in the banking sector. He says he is actively involved in charitable work and volunteers at his local church.

Sophie Torney.summary: Torney is a local councillor and businesswoman who has lived in Kew for almost 30 years. She has previously worked as a software engineer and project manager before transition to running businesses in the financial, technology and literary sectors. She ran as an independent candidate for Kew at the 2022 election, endorsed by an offshoot group of Voices For Kooyong, coming third with a primary vote of 21.1 per cent. Torney served a year-long term as mayor of Booroondara after being elected to council in 2024.

Ann Seeley.summary: Seeley has worked in media, including 13 years at Channel 10 News, and spent five years as a live-in manager and house parent at the Kew Baptist Youth Hostel. She was a founding delegate of Family First and has run for the party in this seat at the last election as well as the federal seat of Menzies at the 2025 election.

Jack Chakoma.summary: Chakoma is a Truganina local and previously operated a support agency for culturally and linguistically diverse Australians.

Vasundhara Kandpal.summary: Kandpal is from the Himalayas and she has worked in research, community education and social welfare for over a decade. Much of her work has been in Melbourne's west alongside multicultural communities, local councils, government agencies and community organisations.

Donna Southern.summary: Southern has worked at the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners and the University of Melbourne, and possesses a PhD in health services research. She says she is a third-generation western-suburbs local and led a campaign for traffic lights at the intersection of Leakes Road and the Western Freeway.

Lee-Ann Elmes.summary: Elmes is the president of Hamilton Youth Victoria and has worked in education. She was the Family First candidate for Wannon at the 2025 federal election.

Dom Bonanno.summary: Bonanno has worked in the technology industry for almost 30 years, has been a councillor on Macedon Ranges Shire council since 2020, and served for a year as mayor from 2024 to 2025. He was the Liberal candidate for this seat at the last state election.

Michael Seton.summary: Seton is a retired superannuation fund executive with 35 years of experience and previously ran the Australian Government Employees Superannuation Trust and Military Super. In the years prior to his retirement in 2024 he consulted across the industry.

David Segal.summary: Segal says he is a retired stockbroker and has previously stood for election four times for the Liberal Democrats and Libertarian Party, at both state and federal elections.

Rafael Camillo.summary: Camillo is a longtime CBD resident who moved to Australia from Brazil almost two decades ago. He was elected to City of Melbourne council in 2024 and serves as the portfolio head for safety and cleaning as well as the deputy for infrastructure. Before his election to council he was the president of the Residents 3000 organisation.

Rob McCathie.summary: McCathie has spent his working life in IT as a computer systems administrator and consultant for small and medium businesses. He is the Libertarian Party's registered officer and has previously stood for election three times, including as a Liberal Democrats candidate for the upper house at the last state election.

Rowan Tuckfield.summary: Tuckfield is a businessman who has worked in credit at banks in Australia and ran a coffee producer in Brooklyn, New York. In the late 1990s he sat on the Premier's Infrastructure Planning Council and he has an economics degree with a major in accounting.

Fiona Adin-James.summary: Adin-James is a qualified and experienced crisis councillor and first began her community services work in neighbourhood houses and community centres in 1990. She has since been involved in disability advocacy, community garden projects, and wellbeing initiatives for elderly communities. She ran as the Animal Justice candidate in this seat at the last state election and as the party's candidate for the federal seat of Hawke at the 2025 election.

Daire Kelly.summary: Kelly works in customer service at an outdoor equipment store and is a delegate for the Retail and Fast Food Workers Union. He moved to Australia from Ireland over a decade ago and has degrees in applied physics and sustainable energy engineering.

Hayden Legro.summary: Legro owns a legal business in Melton and possesses degrees from Monash University, the University of Tasmania, and Catholic Theological College Melbourne. He has been involved in Reclink Australia, a charity providing access to sport to vulnerable and disadvantaged people, for more than 30 years.

Marlene West.summary: West has worked in health care since 1996 and been a registered nurse and mental health nurse. She has also studied communication and counselling, and has a certificate of ministry.

Stella Zigouras.summary: Zigouras is a lawyer and an opera singer. She was the Labor candidate in this seat at the last election.

Noah Briggs.summary: Briggs is a paralegal and earned his law degree from Deakin University. He volunteers at the Eastern Community Legal Centre.

Craig Manners.summary: Manners is the CEO of Orbus Ministries Australia and has 17 years of experience in overseas mission work. He has also worked for more than 40 years in the finance, mining and charity management sectors. Manners was the Family First candidate for Aston at the 2025 federal election and has stood as a Senate candidate for the party.

Alyssa Wormald.summary: Wormald was a founder and inaugural director of the Australian Native Parrot Protection Association, which campaigns against lethal control of parrots and promotes ethical alternatives. She runs a small business with her sister creating eco-friendly, vegan burial shrouds and runs community education sessions on green burial. Wormald ran as the Animal Justice candidate for Bayswater at the 2022 state election.

Rachel Versteegen.summary: Versteegen was a Liberal Democrats candidate for the upper house at the 2022 state election and the Libertarian candidate for Wills at the 2025 federal election.

Natalie Acreman.summary: Acreman was secretary of the RMIT Socialist Alternative and has led the students and youth subgroup of Extinction Rebellion. She was an upper house candidate for the Victorian Socialists at the 2022 state election.

Melissa Goffin.summary: Goffin was a teacher for a decade and served as president of the Victorian Teacher’s Association. She is now managing director of a local restaurant chain on the Mornington Peninsula and has served on the board of small businesses. She was also a founder and organiser of the 2017 Women’s March on Melbourne.

Kerry Macdonald.summary: Macdonald has worked as a senior public servant and a management consultant after beginning her career as a secondary school teacher. She is the president of Labor's Mornington branch and a member of the Labor Environment Action Network.

Adrian Maher.summary: Maher grew up on the Mornington Peninsula and has a professional background in project management and stakeholder engagement.

Fotini Theodossopoulou.summary: Theodossopoulou has a professional background in sales and marketing and worked as an account manager at Fairfax Media. She also helped established a family-owned restaurant and has been involved in small scale residential property development projects.

Asyiqin Sanif.summary: Sanif describes herself as a community activist and proud trade unionist. She is a retail worker and has a degree in communications from RMIT.

Shemane Nathanielsz.summary: Nathanielsz spent 25 years as a registered nurse and serves as a board member of Beaconsfield District Community Bank. She is also the community and business liaison officer in an electorate office.

Josh Utoyo.summary: Utoyo runs a 3D printed goods business and was formerly the Victorian secretary of the Libertarian Party. He was the party's candidate for Menzies at the 2025 federal election.

Lydia Denker.summary: Denker is the founder of Homeschool Academy Australia, a business which says it specialises in personalised education solutions and partners with schools to implement proactive early intervention programs aimed at preventing student disengagement and dropout. She was born in Germany, moved to Australia when she was eight, and was formerly a pop singer and songwriter. Her 2004 single One Perfect Day peaked at 35 on the ARIA charts, and she made it to the final 24 in Australian Idol season four.

Surbhi Snowball.summary: Snowball was born in Mauritius, grew up in India in Zimbabwe, and came to Australia in 2000, moving to the Mornington Peninsula ten years ago. She has run her own business, worked on farms, and now works in finance. She the Labor candidate for Flinders at the 2022 federal election.

Kim Robbins.summary: Robbins has lived on the Mornington Peninsula for six years and was formerly the director and secretary of Voices of Mornington Peninsula. She has worked in marketing for more than 30 years and is the director of a strategic marketing consultancy.

Salomae Haselgrove.summary: Haselgrove grew up on the Fleurieu Peninsula in South Australia and has lived in Melbourne’s inner north for two and a half years. She completed a journalism degree in 2015 and has since worked in journalism and public relations, currently for the Victorian Aboriginal Health Service.

Hsiang-Han Hsieh.summary: Hsieh grew up in the Philippines and migrated to Australia to study biomedicine and medicine at the University of Melbourne. He works as a psychiatrist and ran as the Greens candidate for this seat at the last state election.

Julian Fidge.summary: Fidge is a GP and army veteran who was deployed to East Timor and has undertaken humanitarian work in Rwanda. He was the Liberal Democrats candidate for this seat at the last election as well as the federal seat of Indi at the 2022 election. He was also a candidate for the Country Alliance and Country Party in this seat at the 2014 and 2018 elections, respectively.

Bronwyn Murphy.summary: Murphy is a hospitality worker and studied at La Trobe University.

Kate Hands.summary: Hands has lived in Pakenham for more than 20 years and has a professional background in business, health, social services and local government.

Jacob Andrewartha.summary: Andrewartha is an early childhood educator and has worked as a socialist journalist. He is standing as the candidate for the unregistered Socialist Alliance party and has previously stood for the party in the 2024 Merri-bek City Council.

Kathrine Ashton.summary: Ashton has more than a decade of experience in film, television and theatre and holds a creative arts degree from Swinburne University. She ran as the Family First candidate for the nearby seat of Northcote at the 2022 state election.

Keith Meure.summary: Meure has worked for 25 years in visual effects for film and has a background in theatre, acting, and worship leadership.

Brenton Carbins.summary: Carbins has worked on a farm, in construction, in the public sector, and in technology. He says that one of his businesses created the event management system used by major Australian festivals and the 2000 Sydney Olympic Games.

Lula Tolley.prior_occupation: clerk at a law firm as well as in retail
Lula Tolley.summary: Tolley is a law student at Deakin University and works as a clerk at a law firm as well as in retail.

Hamza Al Katranji.summary: Al Katranji works in healthcare and has worked in Australia, New Zealand, and Saudi Arabia as a surgeon, informatics specialist, and executive. He studied medicine at Alexandria University in Egypt, later earning postgraduate qualifications from Swansea University, Harvard Medical School, and the University of Melbourne. He is also secretary of the Australian Syrian Alliance.

Zheng Chin.summary: Chin is an urban planner with a PhD from Monash University. He has been involved in the Save Preston Market campaign and supported Gaetano Greco's independent campaign for Preston at the 2022 election. Chin ran for Central Ward the 2025 Darebin City Council elections, being narrowly defeated by the Labor candidate.

Charles Aponso.summary: Aponso lives in Melbourne's southeastern suburbs and is a university student who works in hospitality.

Bernadette Gray.summary: Gray is a mother of four, grandmother of nine, and a nurse who has worked in neonatal, aged care, and palliative care.

Megan Read.summary: Read was born in Creswick and raised in Ballarat, and now manages her family farm near Beaufort. She started her own business, Ballarat Myotherapy, at 21 and has served as president of the local Kindergaren, primary school parents club and a childcare working group.

Jo Armstrong.summary: Armstrong is a Tatyoon local and has served on Ararat council since 2016, including five years as mayor. She is also the state president of the Victorian Nationals.

Trevor Andrei.summary: Andrei describes himself as a survival instructor and a former admin of Fox Hunting Australia. He runs his own farm and possesses an electrical spotter qualification.

Jeff Barry.summary: Barry is a CFA volunteer, motorcyclist, skydiver, and recreational hunter and shooter whose roots in the area stretch back four generations. He ran his own arboriculture business in Melbourne for 35 years and was the Libertarian candidate for the federal seat of Mallee at the 2025 election.

Bernard Quince.summary: Quince is a factory worker in Ararat and a former high school science teacher. He ran for this seat at the 2022 state election.

Scott Robson.summary: Robson is a geologist and works as an international mining consultant. He holds a science degree and an MBA, and stood as an independent candidate for the federal seat of Melbourne in 2022.

Shane Sali.summary: Before entering politics, Sali was an accounts manager at the local Telstra business centre and operations manager at a fashion boutique. He was elected to Shepparton council in November 2020 and became mayor in June 2022. Sali has been a board member of Regional Cities Victoria since he became mayor, including two years as chair from 2023 to 2025.

Lou Costa.summary: Costa grew up in Shepparton East and studied landscape architecture at RMIT. She returned to the Goulburn Valley to start her business, Design By Nature, in 1998 and has worked with construction companies in the electorate. She is endorsed by the Voices for Goulburn Valley group.

Freya Hedley.summary: Hedley describes herself as a trans woman working in tech support and hospitality as well as volunteering at a local homeless service.

Ron Nelson.summary: Nelson is a City of Greater Geelong councillor and previously worked in the hospitality industry as a business owner and chef as well as with the Department of Defence. He ran for Liberal preselection in this seat but was defeated by Libby Pettit after previously running as a candidate for the party in Bellarine at the 2014 state election.

Rob Dunstan.summary: Dunstan has been a police officer for more than 30 years and says he has seen the impact of rising crime in the community.

Luan Walker.summary: Walker is a restaurant owner and managing director at an aged care organisation. He is also a justice of the peace and co-founded a wedding services business. He was formerly a member of the Liberal Party and stood as a candidate for the upper house at the last state election.

Nancy Batres-Croes.summary: Batres-Croes was born and raised in Aruba, and has been living in Victoria for 11 years. She has worked in communiucations and marketing as well as being a self-employed pet carer.

Matthew De Angelis.summary: De Angelis is a former startup co-founder and stand-up comedian with more than 15 years’ experience in marketing and creative work. He says his creative work includes educational cartoons about the region, bringing local identity and learning together.

Maria Kerr.summary: Kerr's family migrated from Italy in the 1950s. She has a business management degree and has worked in the insurance industry. Kerr was elected to for the Brimbank City Council in November 2020 where she continues to serve. She was the Liberal candidate for Sydenham at the 2018 state election and for St Albans at the 2022 state election.

Ashleigh Vandenberg.summary: Vandenberg has been a Melton City councillor since 2020 and is a registered nurse specialising in vascular, thoracic and intensive care.

Venkat Ram Upparlapalle.summary: Upparlapalle is a technical consultant and IT design lead at CitiPower and Powercor who has lived in Australia for more than 20 years. He says he has run his own business and a non-profit organisation who is proud to call Tarneit and Wyndham home.

Andrew Elsbury.summary: Elsbury was a Liberal member of the Legislative Council from 2010 to 2014 and left the Liberals in 2022 over what he describes as their “lurch to the right”. Since leaving parliament he has worked in corporate communications, as an electorate officer to then-Corangamite MP Sarah Henderson, and as a project officer at the Australian Industry Group.

Maurita Rahn.summary: Rahn has lived in Tarneit for more than 23 years and was the Animal Justice Party candidate for this seat in 2022. She has a background in procurement, working within the corrections system and health industries, and in her spare time she assists the Victorian Dog Rescue and other wildlife groups, having volunteered and campaigned for animal rights for 18 years.

Leah Van Keulen.summary: Van Keulen has been a teacher for nine years and lives in Werribee and says she has watched parents make hard sacrifices just to put food on the table, keep the lights on or take their child to see a dentist.

Belinda Stojcevski.summary: Stojcevski bought her first hairdressing business at 21 and went on to run two more salons. She says she has raised her two children in the area and has contributed to her local community.

Gavin Trewella.summary: Trewella is a field ecologist and researcher who works casually with an environmental consultancy. He has a PhD in wildlife management from Charles Darwin University.

Rebecca Paterson.summary: Paterson describes herself as a working mother to three daughters.

Vanessa Muradian.summary: Muradian is a sexologist, counsellor, yoga teacher, and owns her own business.

Caleb Schwab.summary: Schwab is a research assistant with a degree in Biomedical Science from Deakin University.

Gav Ronan.summary: Ronan is a business owner, has previously worked as an IT consultant, and runs a family farm. He owned a lodge walk on The Great Ocean Road for 10 years and now runs a tourism business in Ballarat.

Paul Hopper.summary: Hopper is a lifelong Werribee resident who runs a chain of car dealerships in Melbourne’s west and south-west. The suburb of Hoppers Crossing takes its name from his great-great-great grandmother, who lived and worked in the area with her husband in the late 1800s. He has been an independent candidate for this seat at the 2022 state election and the 2025 by-election, polling 14.6 per cent at the latter.

Matthew Emerson.summary: Emerson has worked in telecommunications, media, and IT in the public and private sectors and holds a certificate IV in contact centre operations from Swinburne University. This is his fourth time as a Family First candidate after standing as the party's candidate for Werribee at the 2022 state election and 2025 by-election as well as for Lalor at the 2025 federal election.

Tony Briffa.summary: Briffa served for 10 years on Hobsons Bay council, including two separate year-long terms as mayor. She has worked for the Department of Defence, the Australian Federal Police and the aviation provider for Ambulance Victoria as well as being a justice of the peace and former bail justice.

Gill Gannon.summary: Gannon owns an interior decorating business and is president of the Newport Traders Association. She says she has led a campaign to keep Champion Road open.

Troy Cheers.summary: Cheers describes himself as a proud Richmond fan and keen paintballer.
